guidance.title: How legal adoption works
guidance.subtitle: The official steps and time limits under the Adoption Regulations 2022.
guidance.noteBody: Many websites still show the old 2017 limits (30-day home study, 20-day matching, Rs 40,000). The numbers below are from 2022.

s1.title: Registration
s1.body: Register on CARINGS and state your preferences: child's age group, gender and states.

s3.title: Home Study Report
s3.body: A social worker visits your home and writes the report. It stays valid for 3 years.

s4.title: Waiting list
s4.body: Your place depends on your registration and document dates. For a healthy young child the average wait is about 3 to 3.5 years.

s5.title: Child declared legally free
s5.body: The Child Welfare Committee declares a child legally free for adoption.

s6.title: Child reports
s6.body: The agency uploads the Child Study Report and Medical Examination Report. The Chief Medical Officer certifies the child.
s6.limit: Reports within 10 days; certification within 15 days

s7.title: Referral
s7.body: You are offered a child's reports. You can receive up to 3 referrals, about a month apart.

s8.title: Reservation decision
s8.body: You decide whether to reserve the child.

s9.title: Matching
s9.body: You meet the child and the agency's Adoption Committee approves the match.

s10.title: Pre-adoption foster care
s10.body: The child comes to live with you before the final order.

s11.title: Application to the District Magistrate
s11.body: The agency files the adoption application.

s12.title: Adoption order
s12.body: The District Magistrate decides the application. You get a certified copy within 10 days, and a new birth certificate within 5 days of the order.

s13.title: Follow-up visits
s13.body: A social worker visits every 6 months for 2 years, 4 visits in total.

scam.notConfirmed: This is an automated suspicion. It is not a confirmed finding of fraud.
scam.reportBody: In India, buying or selling a child is a crime. Report it to Childline 1098 or the police.

waitTime.title: Wait-Time Explainer
waitTime.fact1: About 13 waiting parents for every available child (2025 figures, about).
waitTime.fact2: About 65% to 80% of children legally free for adoption have special needs (2024-25, about).
waitTime.fact3: For a healthy young child the average wait is about 3 to 3.5 years.
waitTime.youngNote: Most parents ask for a child under 2 years, so waiting is longest for that group.
waitTime.olderNote: Older children usually wait longer to be adopted, so being open to this age group can matter.
waitTime.openNote: Being open to special needs is your choice. Many children in this group wait for a family.
waitTime.closedNote: It is fine to decide what is right for your family. You can change this later.
waitTime.uncertainty: These are public estimates and not a prediction for you. We do not pressure you to change your preferences.
